source.title: Asymptotics of Wide Convolutional Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including the supplement, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training accuracy for convolutional networks trained from initialization, including on a two-class CIFAR subset. It uses full-batch gradient descent and small binary datasets rather than the version’s broader CIFAR-10/100 benchmark setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports 100% training accuracy for all models in its numerical experiments. Its main scaling results on NTK and test loss, and results cited from other work, are not separate rows about training classification error.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own CNN training-classification results: full-batch gradient descent reaches 100% training accuracy on small binary MNIST and CIFAR-10 subsets. These test V1's training-error outcome in new settings, without reproducing its full benchmark or optimizer recipes.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report 100% training accuracy across their numerical experiments. Their central conclusion is that CNN correlation functions and finite-width corrections follow predicted width scaling; finite-versus-linearized test-loss differences shrink approximately as inverse width, while relative generalization performance depends on stopping time.
record.recipe_differences: Uses full-batch gradient descent on small two-class datasets and studies width scaling; it does not reproduce the broad SGD/Adam benchmark and label-corruption recipes in V1.
record.method_sensitivity: For test loss and accuracy, the finite-width versus linearized model ordering depends on training time and stopping criteria. The paper also reports late-time NTK and loss/accuracy discontinuities for some global-average-pooling models, with timing dependent on depth, width, learning rate, and precision.

fits_no_version.finding: Finite-versus-linearized test-loss gaps shrink approximately as inverse width, and their performance ordering changes with stopping time.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Finite-width CNN generalization approaches linearized-model generalization with an approximately inverse-width gap whose sign can depend on training time.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix D reports late training discontinuities and oscillations in GAP networks, with timing dependent on depth, width, learning rate and numerical precision.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some finite-width GAP CNNs exhibit late training instability sensitive to architecture and numerical settings. No stability threshold or curvature trajectory is measured, so this does not test V5.

record.problems: Training-error evidence is limited to small two-class subsets; the paper does not report separate training-accuracy values by architecture or width. Some late-time global-average-pooling runs exhibit discontinuities and oscillations, which the authors say must be avoided to see the predicted scaling.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately reported training-classification-error results were identified. The finite-versus-linearized test-loss and test-accuracy gaps in Figure 8 do not measure the training-error claim.

untested.parts: Full CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 training sets, corrupted or random labels, SGD or Adam, and comparisons establishing substantial error under smaller models, early stopping or regularized recipes.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious-minimum frequencies, and adding one or two student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation and its prevention through identity shortcuts, special initialization or Fixup.
Comparisons of initialization schemes for learning speed, signal propagation or trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to a measured stability threshold, curvature reduction during recovery, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch normalization versus no normalization for training speed or learning-rate tolerance, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The reported training accuracy establishes reaching zero classification error, not zero squared loss or permanently stable convergence. Appendix D's later fluctuations do not contradict the reported attainment of 100% accuracy.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test CIFAR-100, full 10-class CIFAR-10, corrupted or random labels, SGD or Adam, smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes.
The two-layer teacher-student spurious-minima setting and student-width comparison are not tested.
Does not compare plain and residual networks for depth-related training error or test the cited shortcut, special-initialization, or normalization-free claims.
Does not compare initialization schemes for training speed or trainable depth.
Does not test learning rates above a stability threshold or the catapult and edge-of-stability behaviors.
Does not compare batch normalization with no normalization for training speed or learning-rate tolerance.

rows.subject: one- and three-hidden-layer convolutional neural networks
rows.size_stated: Widths varied; one-hidden-layer models n = [16, 32, ..., 2048], three-hidden-layer models n = [16, 32, ..., 512] in the stated scaling fits
rows.operation_detail: Trained with full-batch gradient descent on 2-class MNIST (0’s and 1’s), with 10 examples per class.
rows.note: Aggregate statement covering the numerical experiments; the paper does not report separate accuracy values for each architecture or width here.
rows.check: The accuracy statement is supported, but the size field uses initialization-scaling fit ranges rather than training-experiment ranges. Section 4.2 and Table 3 also include one-hidden-layer training runs through width 4096. Keep the aggregate accuracy statement distinct from the initialization-only measurements.

rows.subject: four-hidden-layer CNN with tanh activation functions and a flatten before the final dense layer
rows.size_stated: n = 64 and n = 1024 shown for training accuracy; widths n = 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024 shown for loss-gap curves
rows.operation_detail: Trained with full-batch gradient descent on a 2-class CIFAR subset.
rows.note: The setup states all models achieved 100% training accuracy; the section specifies this experiment’s 2-class CIFAR training set.
rows.check: No substantive correction. Section 4 explicitly reports 100% training accuracy for all models; Figure 8 directly plots training accuracy only for widths 64 and 1024.

relationships.condition: One- and three-hidden-layer CNNs on binary MNIST, 10 training examples per class, full-batch gradient descent.
relationships.reason: R1 records the authors' explicit report that all models reached 100% training accuracy, supporting the zero-training-error outcome in this small-data extension.
relationships.display_finding: All tested one- and three-hidden-layer models reached 100% training accuracy.

relationships.condition: Four-hidden-layer tanh CNNs on airplane versus automobile CIFAR-10, 100 training examples per class, full-batch gradient descent.
relationships.reason: R2 records 100% training accuracy; Figure 8 also shows training-accuracy trajectories for widths 64 and 1024. This supports the outcome for the binary subset.
relationships.display_finding: The four-hidden-layer tanh CNNs reached 100% training accuracy on the binary subset.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
